index_record.name: TIED product configuration plane and env policy
index_record.description: Configuration planes (disk, spawn-injected env, CLI session, secrets) with centralized resolution and observability; env is input not authority.

ARCH-TIED_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_POLICY.name: TIED product configuration plane and env policy
ARCH-TIED_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_POLICY.decision: First-party TIED-the-product separates configuration planes: (1) install-managed disk and MCP JSON for global paths and operator toggles; (2) spawn-injected MCP child env as transport only; (3) CLI session env for large payloads and operator texture; (4) secrets in process env never committed to mcp.json. Shell export of global path keys must not override disk authority (delegated to REQ-TIED_RUNTIME_DISK_CONFIG). New production process.env reads require allowlist catalog entry and pass static inventory test. Operational control surfaces prefer MCP tools and CLI commands over undocumented env toggles.

implementation_approach.summary: Allowlist YAML + bootstrap inventory scanner; catalog doc; reuse tied-config-report for observability.
details: tied-env-allowlist-inventory.mjs scans scoped production trees excluding test globs
REQ-TIED_RUNTIME_DISK_CONFIG implements disk/spawn path slice under this umbrella

rationale.why: Umbrella architecture for env policy complements implemented disk resolver without duplicating RDC semantics.
problems_solved: Unbounded env growth without design test
No single configuration plane vocabulary for agents and operators
benefits: Clear spawn vs shell export distinction in vocab and report
